chapter_theme: Songs at Pagai (பாகை): the poet asks to be spared Kama's arrows, women, the begging of patrons, the body's diseases and the burning ground, and asks for Sivayoga and the silent bliss; the praise names Murugan as the Tamil hero who straightened the Pandya's hunch, and describes the town's ponds, groves and towers.
structure_note: A plea against desire and patron-seeking (789), against disease and death (790), and against women for the ocean of silent bliss (791).

789.reading: The poet asks not to faint, sweating and infatuated, under the arrows of Kama, not to go at the bidding of women's fish-like eyes and wither, and not to wander asking who on this serpent-borne earth gives generously, and asks whether he will reach today the feet that ran into the forest the four Vedas seek. The praise names Brahma, Vishnu and Siva who daily wear flowers, Murugan the ruler of walled southern Pagai, the Tamil hero whose tongue spoke the Veda in debate so that the old hunch of the king of Kudal ran away, riding the peacock.
789.nuance: த்யாகம் ஈபவர் யாரென்று அலையாதே: the poet's wandering in search of patrons is set beside desire. நான்மறை நாடும் காடும் ஓடிய தாள் are Murugan's feet that ran in the forest after Valli, which the Vedas search for. கூடலான் முதுகூன் அன்று ஓட is the Pandya Koon (the hunchback) straightened by Sambandar, again Murugan.

790.reading: The poet asks not to waste away with phlegm, fever, chills and wind, not to lose his life in the little nest of the body and go to the burning ground, and not to sink in the fire with brain, bones, nerves and sinews falling apart, and asks Murugan to speak to him so that he may live in the state of Sivayoga called the root. The praise describes Pagai, where fish leap and tear nets in the ponds, ketaki flowers are crushed, areca groves are beaten by the sea and backwaters, and Murugan who loves the peacock.
790.nuance: மூலம் எனும் சிவயோக பதம்: the alternative to the burning body is a state, Sivayoga, not escape. The diseases (ஈளை, சுரம், குளிர், வாதம்) are named first, then the cremation fire that takes the parts of the body. The praise is all landscape.

791.reading: The poet confesses that, drawn to women whose spear-like eyes rush at their earrings and to their musk-scented breasts, he grew infatuated day by day and melted in play, and asks whether his life, whirling amid the waves of the sea, will not sink into the ocean of silent supreme bliss. The praise names Murugan the one who came after the elephant-faced Ganapati with cheeks and trunk, bearer of the bright vel, at Pagai whose towers of coral, emerald, gold and diamond are brushed by the horses of the sun's chariot.
791.nuance: மவுன பரம சுக ... உததி: the ocean of silent supreme joy is set against the sea of waves in which the life whirls, two seas in one plea. The word between (சுகோம கோததி) is hard to divide.
